scenes.b: Night… the Vyasa ashrama held in utter silence. A sage beyond fame… sat alone before the river. Yet his mind… refused to be still.
The very body that told the world what knowledge is… was boiling with the same question. What was it — that emptiness?
As time passed… even the ashrama seemed to decide it must also feel empty to Vyasa. In a house where answers are finished… sometimes an even bigger question takes residence.
The Maharshi who carried knowledge to the world — why could he find no answer for the dissatisfaction in his own heart?
…The wind changed. Somewhere far away… a veena string chimed once. This forest knew — something was about to happen.
At that sound, he lifted his head. Softly. Very, very softly. …It felt — tonight had another reason.
The next morning. The sleeping forest. In the previous part — the ashrama that had made its home with a question… today is awaiting some answer.
Who knew first? This day, the peacocks told it first. The bird did not move. The deer did not move. The whole forest… gazed in one direction.
The light… it came first. In those rays falling on the footpath… even dust was glimmering like little lamps.
…That sound. One single string rang twice. Every role in the play stopped… merely to hear that note.
…That walk. That veena. Every living sound halted and gazed upon the raga… that someone was carrying toward them.
Those steps… have turned the whole world over. And yet it is only where they stop… that peace arrives.
As though the strings resonate by themselves… even before he touches them. Some instruments are played. This one… speaks.
Narada Maharshi. A smile is his first sentence. Story is his second name. The devotee who wanders the worlds — for the first time… is arriving like this, to this ashrama.

He is Narada. The Devarshi. He who travels among worlds singing the name of the Lord. He arrives before anyone calls… he arrives knowing what is about to happen. That walking light today… reaches the Vyasa ashrama.
Hearing that sound, he came out. He looked. It had been a very long time… since he had seen such light within his own courtyard.
Two Maharshis… came into a single light. Reverence in one's eyes… love in the other's smile.
Even when something great is about to happen… Maharshis speak of small things. How is the water… how is the weather.
The honoring of a guest… is divinely ordained. In little Gurudatta's sweet busy-hands, dust-flowers bloomed. Hands clutching a broom with curiosity… loosened from habit.
The disciples brought flower-water for the offering. Narada received it with both hands, reverently. That courtyard… now became the home of conversation.
Narada began his travel tales. The snowy peaks of Kailasa… the seas of light of Vaikuntha… he narrated, smiling throughout. But every now and then… his eyes kept returning to Vyasa.
The smile narrating the story stays the same. But behind that smile… his eyes read Vyasa ever more carefully. In that smile there was… a part that did not add up.
Narada asked — gently, yet directly.
For a while, he did not speak. Even great souls… pause for one breath before they speak of their own greatness.
These hands of mine… divided the immeasurable Veda into four. For the first time, they gave form to formless knowledge. Rig Veda… Yajur Veda… Sama Veda… Atharva Veda.
I wrote the Mahabharata. A hundred thousand verses… I brought an entire world down into letters. Eighteen Puranas — each one a great door.
I taught what dharma is — to thousands of disciples. Those disciples are my family. The letters in which I wrote the laws of dharma… reached every village.
Having said it all… he halted for one moment. To speak of what was done — is easy. To speak of what remains undone — is difficult even for Maharshis.
Narada closed his eyes. That question did not merely come toward him… it entered into him.
He smiled softly. That smile said — I knew your question long before you asked it, Vyasa. That is why I have come.
Narada worked a small miracle.
Gurudatta's hidden giggle slipped out. The story was on track now. As that giggle faded… Narada began to speak of the root cause.
You have knowledge… but your heart is still like parched earth. Parched earth does not need penance… one rain is enough.
After the rain falls… the earth forgets its cracks. The heart too — let the rain of love for the Lord fall… and its cracks close by themselves.
Knowledge glows like a lamp. But what pours ghee into it daily to keep it burning… is that very love, that very remembrance. With it, the lamp flames even higher.
However great a river may be… until it stops falling short, it finds no contentment. The heart is the river… the Lord is the ocean.
People search for something… indoors, outdoors, in the hedges. At last… even the lamp smiles — what you seek was in your hand all along.

What must be done? Listening — to His leelas. Remembering — not imagining… but gently recalling. Singing — even if the voice cracks… singing truly. That is all. There is no greater doctrine than this.
Then — Vyasa bent forward. Not like an author… but like a child. If one must understand… that bend is everything.
Narada tapped his veena softly.
The ashrama smiled — slowly, but with one heart. Speak — of His glories. Of His leelas. Of devotees who love Him. And what change comes into the hearts of those who listen — speak of that too.
However dark the night may be… morning transforms it. This heart is the same. Not hours of practice… one true word is enough.
Then Vyasa asked the true question. Narada's eyes… traveled to some old, long-ago morning.
Very long ago… a servant woman's home. A boy walking with his mother for the sake of his hunger. His name then was different — but those eyes… are today's Narada's.
The mother toiled the whole day… yet kept putting half of her own share of food into that boy's plate. A poor house — but a courtyard filled with love.
That day — sages arrived in that village. Not for food. Not for water. Only to rest a short while. And yet — that short while changed a life.
In that house, the only thing that could be offered was — service. The boy carried water… his hands trembled, but his eyes drank only of the sages' faces.
Past midnight, the boy still did not stir. The stories of Narayana — rang like strings within his little heart. That night, a seed fell into his heart… bhakti.
They went — yet they remained. The boy's eyes now kept turning toward the path they had taken. Upon his lips, now just one name… Narayana.
Then one morning… that home fell silent and alone. The mother's hands would work no more — the vessels, the broom, everything told it. Even in the lives of Maharshis… such mornings come.
Alone, he took to the road. One change of clothes. A small bundle on his shoulder. Even tears could not hold him back — that name the sages had spoken alone guided his steps.
He walked many days. Beneath the shade of a peepal tree, he closed his eyes. His heart filled with one name only. Then… before him — light. A light filled only with love.
And that light said…

The boy smiled — through his tears. That very smile… is today's Narada's. Bhakti is like that — it turned that servant's boy into a sage. All I received was that love. All that my veena sings is that very tale.
Now… it is your turn. The duty to carry the nectar of bhakti to the world is yours, Vyasa. Your pen must now write… His glories alone.
Speak — of His virtues. Speak — of His leelas. Speak — of devotees who weep for Him, and of those who smile too. Speak — of how the heart transforms merely by listening.
Then Vyasa rose. Those shoulders that always stood for the world… this time rose for a new writing.
He left the way he had come. But inside that ashrama… nothing would ever be the same. Everywhere the eyes turned — that story remained.
The same courtyard. The same ancient banyan. On a night of ten thousand questions… one single answer. That changed everything.
Vyasa Maharshi began to comprehend his lack… there was knowledge… there was dharma… but the supreme nectar of devotion to the Lord must yet be delivered to the world in fullness.

That evening… the river spoke another language. The same language it had always spoken — but now he understood it. Answers are not sought far away… where there is devotion — they arrive into your very hand.
That night — he sat and shaped his own future. How the new temple should begin… he built it within that night's contemplation.
He sat again. The same seat. The same closed-eyes moment. But this time… within, there is no emptiness. A smile — is approaching. From very far — all the way to the Supreme Soul.

Those words spoken by Narada Maharshi… kindled a new resolve in Vyasa's heart. What would be born of that resolve… is not merely a scripture — an amrita-stream of devotion, knowledge and renunciation… Srimad Bhagavatam.
In the next part… how did creation begin? From where did Brahma receive that knowledge? Subscribe… that story — is about to be born.
